collisions.trigger: Every src/flask/*.py file imports 'typing as t' (stdlib), which the resolver records as importPath='typing', clause='typing'.

determinism_check.method: Two graphi rebuilds of the same flask pin, snapshots compared at the SQLite row count level.
determinism_check.note: The snapshot sha256s differ across the two runs because the snapshot envelope embeds a timestamp; the CONTENT counts (nodes, edges, by-kind) are byte-identical. F5 is reproducible: the spurious typing edges appear in every rebuild with the same count.

f5_measurement.decision: RE-GRADE per SW-181 AC-9: the measurement fails to support GA at cross-file-heuristic, so Python is RE-GRADED — NOT declared at the same level. The re-grade is recorded as a follow-on product-byte change (PYTHONFANOUT-001, see below).
f5_measurement.mechanism: For an import 'import typing as t' (path='typing'), pyClause returns 'typing' as the lookup key. clausePackageFileNodes iterates idx.byClause['typing'] which contains every directory whose base name is 'typing'. flask's 'tests/typing/' declares the 'typing' clause; clausePackageFileNodes therefore returns ALL file nodes under 'tests/typing/', and the resolver emits imports edges to every one — including to test files that nothing in src/flask/* imports.
f5_measurement.question: Does Python's package-import resolution fan out over colliding directory clauses (the F5 finding, PARITY-002 shape)?
f5_measurement.shape: clausePackageFileNodes emits an imports edge for every file node in every directory declaring the import-path's trailing segment as package clause. ADR 0009 fixed this for Go (module-relative directory lookup); Python still uses clause-keyed lookup via pyClause → clausePackageFileNodes.
f5_measurement.verdict: F5 IS REAL on flask: Python's package-import resolution does fan out over colliding directory clauses. The fan-out shape is identical to PARITY-002 (Go's pre-ADR-0009 defect), and the fix direction is the same module-aware keying.

implication_for_ga.evidence_row_change: G4 stays UNKNOWN with 'current' rewritten to state the F5 failure and 'evidence_uri' pointed at this measurement file. The 'sha' stays empty: UNKNOWN cannot carry a sha because the F5 measurement finds a defect rather than supports GA.
implication_for_ga.f5_outcome: FAILED — flask carries a 'typing' clause collision that the python resolver fans out over
implication_for_ga.sw181_ac9_routing: Re-grade Python rather than declare. Re-grade is the responsibility of SW-181 AC-9 follow-on (PYTHONFANOUT-001 fix). SW-192 only PUBLISHES the measurement, FILES the defect, and updates the G4 evidence row.
